recap:
## Decisions
- Include a remote-locator ("finder") function. [00:14:53]
- No speech recognition, because it is hard to program, risks false triggers from TV audio, and is costly. [00:15:32]
- The locator will be a two-part package: a separate sender stuck on the TV or wall sends a radio signal to the remote. [00:16:28]
- The remote beeps when located; no light is needed. [00:17:26]
- The target group stays teenagers and young professionals, even without speech recognition. [00:16:45]
- The idea of a "home" or holder for the remote is set aside for now. [00:17:02]
- The remote gets a dedicated power button. Using a held-down number button for power was rejected as confusing. [00:19:42]

## Action items
- PM: Put meeting minutes in the shared documents folder and finish the pending ones before next time [00:01:07]
- All: Finish the questionnaire [00:25:53]
- All: Do 30 minutes of individual work after lunch and bring new ideas to the next meeting [00:26:02]

## Unresolved
- Whether to replace number buttons with an iPod-style scroll wheel or touchpad, and how channel and volume would be separated on it. [00:23:02]
- Whether a scroll wheel would make the remote too expensive. [00:23:18]
- Whether to include DVD controls. The PM is unsure whether "television only" excludes DVD, and the ME noted DVD players have their own remotes. [00:24:50]
- Whether to add a mode-switch button so the touchpad works for both TV and DVD. This was deferred for further thought. [00:25:48]
